correctness.rationale: The attached complete RESULT.md replaces the false attachment description with the forest bijection, isolates the all-root boundary d=n-1 and supplies an explicit strict-minor proof. Fix the prescribed path and then a chain of length h from w to a root. Absorbing the chain vertices expands the root set from q=d+1 to q+h; the reduced Laplacian nI-J on the remaining m vertices has determinant (q+h)n^(m-1), interpreted as 1 at m=0. This gives the telescoping depth tail; multiply by the probability (n-d-1)/(n-2) of missing the path. Each feasible positive-depth endpoint has the same completion count. In the Pascal network an inverted matching intersects, and for the order-preserving matching the early-rise paths of heights min(h_i,x+k_i) are strictly separated on their common abscissas, including h_i=0. For the mass ratio, both factors at positive h decrease; the atom at 0 gives the larger ratio, including the direct support comparison when d=1. The h=1 survival strictly decreases for every adjacent d, which combined with stochastic order gives strict negative covariance by the independent-copy identity. These checks include n=3 and the terminal deterministic law.

Enumerates edge sets of size n-1 on n=3..6, filters by connectivity, and checks all conditional survival tails and projection counts for each prescribed off-path geodesic and depth. For n=6 the denominators by d are 432,432,288,120,24. The frozen Prüfer checker was inspected, not executed; the all-n proof is not inferred from either enumeration.

evidence: Aldous–Pitman, TR526, Lemma 5 eq. (6), PDF p. 6, gives the law of the prescribed marked subtree in the more general p-tree model. At equal weights the probability of a fixed feasible subtree with d+h+1 vertices is (d+h+1)/n^(d+h); summing over labels and projection positions recovers the finite depth counts.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Credit this stronger coverage of the underlying probability law. It does not give an order across the conditioning distances; one must regroup into tails, identify the Pascal kernel with correct row orientation and show a distinct mass-kernel comparison. No general ordering theorem for marked subtrees here was established.

value.rationale: The third-vertex pendant depth is a canonical component of three-point geometry. Knowing exactly which all-order tail minors are positive and comparing successive conditional mass laws in likelihood-ratio order is substantially more informative than the raw count, a marginal distribution or the sign of one covariance; it gives strict negative association for arbitrary increasing functions of the two statistics. The contribution is confined to this uniform finite model.
